direction.doc: vertical = the frame is split into vertical strips, each offset up or down, with RGB separated vertically; horizontal = split into horizontal strips, offset left or right

slices.doc: Number of strips (rounded); each strip's width is randomized per step

amount.doc: Maximum strip offset, as a fraction of the canvas short side; about 15% of strips are additionally enlarged 2.5× (tearing)

rgb.doc: RGB channel separation distance, as a fraction of the canvas short side

steps.doc: Number of steps (rounded) over which the random values are re-rolled during the transition; within a step the frame does not move, and it jumps as a whole between steps, giving the glitch its stuttering rhythm

flicker.doc: Flash: on each step, the whole frame is brightened with probability flicker × intensity; 0 = no flash

doc: Digital glitch transition. Step index b = ⌊p × steps⌋; all random values for this step are taken from splitmix64(seed, b × 2²⁰ + slot index); intensity I = 1 − |2p − 1|. Along the strip axis, slices strips are cut with weights of 0.3 + rand; each strip is offset with probability 0.2 + 0.7I by round((2·rand − 1) × amount × I × (tearing ? 2.5 : 1)) px, and takes the incoming frame with probability q = clamp((p − 0.25)/0.5, 0, 1), otherwise the outgoing frame. Sampling clamps at the canvas edges (pixels pulled out past the edge drag out the edge pixels as a smear). R and B are each offset by ±round(rgb × I × (0.5 + rand)) px along the offset axis, and alpha takes the maximum of three samples. The whole frame is brightened with probability flicker × I by 0.35 × I × flicker (c' = c + (α − c)·f). Only integer offsets and nearest-pixel moves are used, with no transcendental functions; progress = 0 / 1 is byte-identical to from / to. Recommended dur 0.25–0.35 s (when dur is not set, the transition default of 0.4 s applies).
